messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — onboarding reranker-v2 int8 PTQ shows weird signal split by doc source. overall NDCG up but MRR down, and the drop is concentrated in the internal KB cohort.

maya: Eval command: `./eval_rerank --model reranker-v2-int8 --dataset combined_holdout --cohorting source --seed 42 --batch 128`

maya: Summary numbers (float -> float):
```
overall NDCG@10: 0.412 -> 0.428 (+0.016)
overall MRR@10: 0.332 -> 0.320 (-0.012)
kb cohort NDCG@10: 0.398 -> 0.410 (+0.012)
kb cohort MRR@10: 0.381 -> 0.345 (-0.036)
web cohort MRR@10: 0.314 -> 0.329 (+0.015)
```

maya: Anyone seen this pattern where NDCG increases but MRR (top-hit metrics) drop for a specific source? suspect some top-ranked ties broken differently after quantization, or tokenizer/batching parity.

owen: Do we normalize candidate scores per-query? Or are we rescaling across the whole eval? That can change MRR more than NDCG. Also can you paste an example query + candidate list where top changed?

maya: We do per-query softmax over scores. Example (sanitized):
```
query: "how to connect redwood to internal db"
candidates (pre -> post):
1) kb_doc_123 (score 14.2 -> 13.1)
2) web_doc_990 (13.9 -> 13.9)
3) kb_doc_456 (13.6 -> 13.6)
```

maya: On several cases the top kb doc drops 1 rank after PTQ even though relative scores look close.

li: Two quick checks: 1) stratify by doc length/token count; short KB docs sometimes lose margin with int8. 2) check tokenizer padding/truncation parity between reranker and candidate prep — mismatch can shift scores.

sam: Also run MRR@1 / Precision@1. NDCG can be robust to small reordering but MRR@1 will highlight top-hit loss. If both MRR@1 and MRR@10 drop, it's a top-rank problem.

maya: Ran quick extra metrics: MRR@1 dropped similarly for kb cohort (0.287 -> 0.250). So top-hit loss confirmed.

eval-bot: New eval artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-evals/reranker-v2/int8/onboard/3918204380/artifacts.tar.gz (contains per-query diffs + candidate score CSV).

owen: Proposed experiment plan:
- A) rerun with candidate score rescaling (multiply logits by 0.95) to test numeric headroom effect.
- B) seq_len ablation: clamp candidate side to 128 vs 512 and compare.
- C) regen embeddings / tokenization using same tokenizer binary as production (no pip-installed tokenizers mismatch).
- D) bootstrap CIs on KB cohort (1000 resamples) to check significance.

maya: Assigning: owen -> A, li -> B + tokenizer parity check, sam -> D (bootstrap CI). I'll run deterministic seeds + kv-cache disabled to rule out nondeterminism.

sam: Got it. I'll share a small notebook for bootstrap code (stratified by query) and attach the CI bands. Expect ~30-60m runs on small farm.

li: I'll also run a small local ablation that turns off per-query softmax and uses raw scores to inspect margin distributions. Might reveal whether quantization compresses score variance.

maya: Thanks. If we confirm top-hit loss, mitigation options: temperature rescale, small post-PTQ calibration (linear bias/rescale), or fall back to fp16 for KB-sensitive traffic. We'll reconvene with numbers in the morning. :thumbsup:
